clue.text: Disinfectant from almost full bottle applied to tailless vermin

indicators.note: almost says the word for the bottle stops one letter short of its end

parts.note: a carboy is a big glass bottle, here full-sized

indicators.note: tailless says the vermin word loses its final letter

parts.note: lice are parasitic vermin

explanation.surface: Someone makes a cleaning agent by pouring a nearly full bottle over rats with no tails.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims CARBOY to CARBO; 'tailless' trims LICE to LIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Carbolic acid, or phenol, was the classic antiseptic soap ingredient, a standard household germ-killer.

clue.text: A way of running spy network that dispenses with locks?

parts.note: a lope is a long easy running stride
the CIA is the American spy agency

explanation.surface: A spy ring that has given up picking locks.
explanation.definitionFit: A medical condition causing hair loss, so the sufferer goes without tresses.

clue.text: Agile brute takes on the Great Stone Face

indicators.note: agile suggests nimble movement, so the letters dance into a new order

explanation.surface: A nimble thug confronts a famously expressionless face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Agile' rearranges BRUTETAKESON. The Great Stone Face was the nickname of the deadpan silent-film comedian.
explanation.definitionFit: The nickname given to the silent-film star for his famously unsmiling deadpan expression.

clue.text: Dressing protecting disabled part of body

indicators.note: protecting means the dressing word wraps round the disabled word

parts.note: lint is a fabric used for dressing wounds
game is an old word for lame, as in a game leg

explanation.surface: A bandage shields an injured bit of anatomy.
explanation.definitionFit: A tough band of tissue binding bones together at a joint.

clue.text: Company tries for an audience, and works together well

indicators.note: for an audience says the word must be listened to, not read

parts.note: a judge hears or tries a case

explanation.surface: A theatre company rehearses for the public and gels as a team.
explanation.walkthrough: A court 'tries' or 'hears' a case; 'for an audience' signals the sound-alike HERES.
explanation.definitionFit: Hangs together as a unified, consistent whole.

clue.text: It may be necessary when visiting Lisbon

definitions.text: It may be necessary when visiting Lisbon

parts.words: It may be necessary when visiting Lisbon
parts.note: something a traveller to the Portuguese capital needed before the euro: the local cash

explanation.surface: Advice for a trip to Portugal.
explanation.definitionFit: This was the currency unit of Portugal until the euro replaced it.

clue.text: Really fit

explanation.definitionFit: As an interjection it expresses surprise like 'indeed'; as an adjective it means healthy.

clue.text: Girl coming in before time, not having pound for the messenger

indicators.note: coming in says the girl word enters the other word
not having says the pound letter is dropped

parts.note: early means before the expected time
L is the abbreviation for pound, from libra
a miss is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl arrives early, without a pound to pay the courier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not having' drops the pound letter from the word for 'before time', and 'coming in' then puts the girl inside what is left; 'for the' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy sent on a mission to deliver a message or represent someone.

clue.text: No turning back the flow of liquid in operation

indicators.note: turning back says the little word No is read the other way round

parts.note: a stream is a flow of liquid

explanation.surface: No reversing the current of a liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning back' flips the word No; 'the flow of liquid' looks like part of the definition but is wordplay, with 'in operation' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Industrial jargon: a plant that has come on stream is running and productive.

clue.text: Plant left undisturbed by landslide?

parts.note: the proverb says a rolling stone gathers none of this plant, so a slide of tumbling rocks would leave it untouched

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders which plant would survive a landslip.
explanation.walkthrough: Plays on the proverb 'A rolling stone gathers no ...': a landslide is a lot of rolling stones.
explanation.definitionFit: A small, low green plant growing on rocks and damp ground, the one named in the rolling-stone proverb.

clue.text: Traditional scheme's return added to export profitability

parts.note: trad is the short form of traditional, as in trad jazz

indicators.note: return here says the scheme word comes back to front

parts.note: a ruse is a scheme or trick
plus means added to

explanation.surface: An old-fashioned plan's yield boosts the profit made on goods sold abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'return' turns the scheme word round to give ESUR; 'added' reads like a link but supplies its own synonym.
explanation.definitionFit: A country earns more from sales abroad than it spends on imports, an excess on the balance of exports.

clue.text: Straightforward trips by sand-yacht?

explanation.definitionFit: Means easy progress without obstacles; humorously, also voyages across flat open ground in a wind-powered land vehicle.

clue.text: Hard to get caught in a fright

indicators.note: in says the caught letter goes inside the word for a fright

parts.note: a scare is a fright
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone is hard to pin down because they were caught in a moment of panic.
explanation.definitionFit: Something in short supply is difficult to obtain.

clue.text: I go mad with a name (my own obsesses me)

indicators.note: mad suggests the letters go wild and get rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone confesses to going crazy over a name, namely their own.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' rearranges IGO and ANAME; 'with' just joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: Obsessive self-absorption: a person fixated on themselves, the parenthesis spoken in that person's voice.

clue.text: A range of colours is allowed in paste form

indicators.note: in places the allowed word inside the paste word

parts.note: pâté is food in paste form
let means allowed, as in 'let off'

explanation.surface: A set of shades is permitted when made up as paste.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is allowed' looks like part of the definition's grammar, but it is the inserted piece; 'in' places it.
explanation.definitionFit: An artist's board holds the selection of paints in use, and by extension a set of hues.

clue.text: Prince comes in to affix medal for sport

parts.note: to pin is to affix

indicators.note: comes in says the prince letter enters the medal word

parts.note: gong is British slang for a medal

explanation.surface: A prince arrives to pin a decoration on a sporting champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gong' is British slang for a medal or decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Table tennis, a game played with small bats over a net on a table.

clue.text: Look — wet washing!

parts.note: la is an old exclamation meaning look or behold
undry means not dry, so wet

explanation.surface: Someone points out a pile of damp clothes.
explanation.walkthrough: LA is an archaic exclamation used in crosswords for 'look'.
explanation.definitionFit: The clothes and linen to be cleaned, or just cleaned, collectively called the wash.

clue.text: Mechanical actors in RUR?

parts.note: Čapek's play R.U.R. introduced robots, so its cast is machinery, and 'mechanical actors' recalls Shakespeare's rude mechanicals

explanation.surface: A review of the cast of a Czech science-fiction play.
explanation.walkthrough: R.U.R. is Karel Čapek's 1920 play that coined the word robot.
explanation.definitionFit: Self-operating machines that imitate living beings, like robots.

clue.text: Materiel has been ordered, as it happens

indicators.note: has been ordered means the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: Military equipment has been requisitioned, as it turns out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has been ordered' rearranges MATERIEL; 'as it happens' looks like a throwaway phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: Computing term for processing with no delay, live at the moment events occur.

clue.text: Have groups of cowboys Sheriff at the front?

parts.note: posses are bands of riders raised by a sheriff

indicators.note: at the front picks the opening letter of the word Sheriff

explanation.surface: A Western asks whether the gangs of cowboys have the sheriff leading them.
explanation.definitionFit: To own or hold something.

clue.text: Almost nothing free of charge?

explanation.walkthrough: 'free of charge' reads like 'gratis' but means electrically neutral.
explanation.definitionFit: This subatomic particle has a near-zero mass and carries no electric charge at all.

clue.text: The papers here need looking at within a year

definitions.text: The papers here need looking at within a year

parts.words: The papers here need looking at within a year
parts.note: the office tray where unread documents wait their turn, joking that a slow bureaucrat takes a year to clear it

explanation.surface: A complaint about a sluggish office.
explanation.definitionFit: A desk tray holding incoming correspondence awaiting attention.

clue.text: Sovereignty resides in brown emperor

indicators.note: resides in says the sovereignty word lives inside the colour word

parts.note: tan is a brown shade
the Raj was British sovereignty over India

explanation.surface: Royal power lies with a sun-browned ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Trajan was a Roman emperor of the second century AD.

clue.text: It's ample (when developed) to go round prescribed course — in solar system?

indicators.note: to go round says the developed letters surround the course word
when developed means the letters grow into a new arrangement

parts.note: a lane is a set course, as for a runner or a ship

explanation.surface: A generous route somewhere among the planets.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue ran over a column break in the paper. 'when developed' rearranges the letters of It's ample into PTESIMAL, and 'to go round' wraps them round the course.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiny rocky bodies that clumped together to form planets in the early solar system, so they are found there.

clue.text: Pub lacks leadership — needs mine host

indicators.note: lacks leadership says the pub word loses its first letter

parts.note: a bar is a pub
my means mine, belonging to me

explanation.surface: A leaderless pub needs a landlord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mine host' looks like a pub landlord, but 'host' alone is the definition, a large multitude.
explanation.definitionFit: A host is a great number, especially of soldiers, as in 'heavenly host'.

clue.text: Flag of Eire — that's not hard

indicators.note: not says the hard letter is taken away

parts.note: Irish means of Eire, Ireland
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Ireland's national flag with something hard left out.
explanation.definitionFit: The yellow flag is a wild iris, a waterside plant, so a flag is this flower.

clue.text: Here are two of the Roman persuasion, DV

definitions.text: Here are two of the Roman persuasion, DV

parts.words: Here are two of the Roman persuasion, DV
parts.note: the letters D and V stand for 500 and 5 in the Roman system, so they are of the Roman persuasion as figures, not as Catholics

explanation.surface: Two Roman Catholics are introduced, with 'Deo volente' tagged on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Roman persuasion' suggests Catholics and DV the Latin 'God willing', but D and V are Roman figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Symbols that represent numbers, such as the letters used for figures in ancient Rome.

clue.text: Odds on fishes having what look like glittering scales?

parts.note: SP is the starting price, the betting odds at a race's start
angles means fishes with rod and line

explanation.surface: Betting on an angler's catch with shimmering scales.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (starting price) is the racing term for odds; 'on' and 'having' join the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Small shiny discs sewn on clothing, which do resemble the gleaming scales of a fish.
